newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Old Mutual plans Africa's biggest shopping complex.
newsitem.headline: Old Mutual plans Africa's biggest shopping complex.

text.p: South Africa's Old Mutual Properties said on Friday it planned Africa's biggest property development to date, a three billion rand shopping complex situated between Johannesburg and Pretoria.
The centre, on a 65 hectare site at Midrand, will be three times the size of the giant Sandton City development in Johannesburg's northern suburbs.
Work on the Zonk'izizwe Shopping Resort (which means all nations) was expected to start at the end of the year and be completed by mid-2000. The site has already been acquired.
Old Mutual Properties, the property arm of the country's biggest investment group, said it was currently negotiating with potential foreign partners whose participation could speed up the project.
The centre will include shops, hotels, an entertainment complex and a waterfront development.
It will also have arts and crafts districts, residential and office accomodation and gardens set among three lakes, each of which will surround an adventure island.
"Zonk'izizwe is part of an initiative for the new millenium," Ian Watt, head of Old Mutual Properties told a news briefing.
He said the complex was spearheaded a programme of major development by Old Mutual.
"This will not just be a shopping centre but a total experience with a host of options for shopping, dining and amusement...a play centre for everyone," Watt said.
Features include interactive play and recreation areas as well as learning centres such as museums, an aviary, botanical gardens and an aquarium.
The project was featured at an international property market in France last month, drawing "substantial foreign interest", Watt said.
"We're giving high priority to the need to attract foreign retailers to give the project a slightly different experience. There have been and will be ongoing discussions," he said.
The speed with which the project was completed would depend on the involvemnet of other partners.
The group has so far been in talks with major international and South African hotel groups, Watt said.
The development will be on land stretching from Grand Central Airport to the Midrand town centre and is a 20 minute drive from Johannesburg International airport.
It will offer parking for 15,000 cars.
Watt said Midrand -- which has been proposed as a parliamentary site -- was fast becoming an important focal point in South Africa and represented an exciting place for development.
Hans Jooste, chief executive officer of Midrand's metropolitan local council, said the project would provide a considerable boost to the Midrand and overall economy.
"Midrand is in the throes of a potential property development boom valued at over 10 billion rand...and the development lends further weight to our bid to have parliament in Midrand," he said.

The project would most likely generate around 4,000 permanent jobs and 6,000 jobs in the local construction industry, another local council representative said, providing much needed employment for residents of the nearby Ivory Park squatter camp.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
